images.title: Rectangle from three squares
images.purpose: Show a rectangle 9 cm by 3 cm made of three equal squares of side 3 cm.
images.composition: One long rectangle centred, split by two vertical lines into three equal squares, with a bracket below.
images.exact_structure: One rectangle 9 units wide and 3 units tall, outline teal #0072B2, split by two grey #6B7280 vertical lines into exactly 3 equal squares. Outer squares plain, middle square shaded light amber #E69F00. Bottom bracket spanning the full width labelled 9 cm; left side labelled 3 cm. Exactly 1 rectangle, 3 squares, 2 splitting lines.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
two squares or four squares, or unequal squares
images.takeaway: Three squares in a row make a rectangle three times as long as wide.
images.description: Rectangle 9 cm by 3 cm divided into three equal squares of side 3 cm.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the squares and say how many sides long the rectangle is.

image_decisions.why: One clean geometry picture carries the single idea of this video.
